findings.statement: a purpose-built segment writer's floor is at least 3x the general put path
findings.detail: the floor writes 1660878 keys/s against the store writer's 805911 -- 2.06x (bulk-parts vs store-writer: greater 2.061x (p=0.0022, rel_iqr 68.8%/28.4%)), 0.60s a million against 1.24s. segwrite-plan.md registered 3x as the bar worth a second writer in the format layer and 5x as clearly worth it. The floor omits the block table, the checksums and the superblock, so a real writer lands above it

findings.statement: building the index is the smaller half of what a bespoke writer must do
findings.detail: `flatindex::encode` over 1000000 keys takes 0.104s of the floor's 0.602s, 17.2%. A checkpoint already pays this and no writer can skip it, so if it dominated there would be little left to win

notes: two arms interleaved over the same sorted input, one value a key -- the shape a seal has after its sort. store-writer is what a seal does today; bulk-parts is the floor a purpose-built writer could reach and NOT an implementation of one: it omits the block table, the checksums and the superblock, so a real writer lands above it
predictions registered in segwrite-plan.md before the run
